_comment: THE FEEDBACK-TIME BUDGET PER GATE PROFILE (#1020). Down-only: `budgetSeconds` is a ceiling and may only fall. `cargo xtask gate` fails a profile whose steps together overran it and prints the per-step timing table, and the `ledgers` step in every profile refuses a commit that raises any number in this directory. The numbers were RE-BASED ONCE, on 2026-09-12, under an owner ruling recorded as D-1020-B2 in docs/decisions.md — the workspace the wave-1 numbers were seeded from held one crate and now holds nine, and an owner ruling is the only legitimate way a number in a down-only ledger rises. They are down-only again from this baseline. Every entry states its measurement and the headroom multiplier that produced it; `nightly` and `release` stay unbounded by ruling, written as null because a null is not a number and so cannot be ratcheted. The measurement is quoted in `headroom` rather than stored as a second number, for the same reason compile-time.json does it: a ceiling pinned to today's workspace would fail the gate the first time a crate landed, and the author would learn to widen ledgers. Keyed by hardware class in the vocabulary of tests/journeys.json. v0's ledgers live under tests/ and retire with v0; these are v1's.

ci-linux-x64-4c.headroom: KEPT at 120 s in the 2026-09-12 re-base, because the measurement sits under a third of it: `cargo xtask gate --profile local` on a WARM tree is 24.0 s of 120 s at nine workspace members and 41.6 s at ten, on this 4-vCPU container (fmt 0.7, clippy 1.4, test 39.4, rules and ledgers 0.0). This budget is scored on a warm tree and nothing else (D-1020-B2-1): the 120 s promise is the developer's feedback time after an edit, not the first build after a clone, and a COLD run is charged against `coldLocalProfileSeconds` in compile-time.json instead. The gap is for the crates wave 2b adds — vault, seat, core, core-ffi, sim, media and the turmoil suite — and it is the thing that forces the issue's structural answers (one crate per app, mold or lld, sccache, optimised dependencies in the dev profile) rather than letting the edit-run loop rot quietly. Wave 1 measured 4.9 s for a workspace of one crate; almost all of today's number is `cargo test --workspace` over 371 tests.

RAISED 900 s -> 1500 s under the owner's 2026-09-12 ruling (D-1020-B2-3), to what the measurement needs and no further: `cargo xtask gate --profile pr` measured 1420.1 s on a COLD tree at nine members — test 1072.1, clippy 54.7 (off a check-warm tree; 587.6 from empty), release-build 240.3, ts-static 25.3, secrets 16.9, everything else under 6 s each. Multiplier 1.06, i.e. the next round number above the measurement and no more, because this is the one profile the rung table binds and headroom here is bought by structural work rather than by a bigger ledger. The same profile on a WARM tree is 575.8 s, and CI restores a Cargo cache (`target/` plus `~/.cargo/bin`, gate.yml), so a cache HIT is the normal case and 1420 s is the cache-miss tail: against #892's rung-2 wall clock of 15 minutes (docs/decisions.md G-lane-rules, 15/45/90/300 minutes) the p95 this profile spends is the warm run, and this ceiling is the tail it must not exceed. gate.yml's job `timeout-minutes` rose to 40 to sit above it, because a run the runner kills cannot report the budget it is scored against. Wave 2b's crates are charged here — the issue rules the turmoil schedules onto every pull request — and Kotlin/Gradle is NOT: it has its own `mobile-jvm` row.

Unbounded by ruling, unchanged by the 2026-09-12 re-base. Wave 1 measured 8.7 s warm, of which the v0 oracle suite is 4.9 s. The device lanes it will carry run on a self-hosted macOS runner with attached phones, where the wall clock is bounded by the hardware and not by a budget.

Unbounded by ruling. Wave 3 lane G's VPS smoke is the remaining deliberate FAILURE, so the profile still cannot pass vacuously. Wave 2 lane R's restore drill is real as of #1020 and is the other step that dominates the profile.
ci-linux-x64-4c._provenance: restore-drill measured 18.2 s through `cargo xtask gate --profile release` on ci-linux-x64-4c (#1020, wave 2 lane R), and 3.9 s as a warm `cargo test -p centraid --test restore_drill`. It founds a vault, enrols a seat, writes 12 commits, takes a generation, DELETES the live data directory, runs the real `centraid recover` into a fresh one, compares 247 tables and 209 rows, and proves the old seat is told epoch-mismatch, re-pairs and converges. Recorded as EVIDENCE, not as a ceiling: `budgetSeconds` for this profile is null by ruling, there was no restoreDrillSeconds slot to fall, and a ceiling invented from one run is a number a later author would learn to widen. Each run writes its own number to target/xtask/release/restore-drill/timing.json.

ci-linux-x64-4c.headroom: MEASURED AND SET by wave 3 lane E, written here when the step became real (#1020 wave 3 lane X3; the measurement is contracts/handoff/E/measured.md). Three consecutive `./gradlew mobileJvm` runs took 91 s, 15 s and 16 s on this container — the first compiling Kotlin from cold, the other two over a warm Gradle build cache; a fourth run from a clean `mobile/build` with `--no-daemon` and the wrapper distribution already on disk took 141 s. 420 s is roughly three times that cold number, which is what a fresh CI container pays: a Gradle distribution download, a cold Kotlin compile, a cold `cargo build -p centraid-core-ffi` and the fixture vault. A budget sized on the 16 s warm number would red on the first run of every container, which is the one run that always happens. Kotlin/Gradle JVM tests are still not charged to `pr` (D-1020-B2-3): a different toolchain with a different cold cost, and one number answering for two build systems is a number that answers for neither. Down-only from here.
